# Printing press

> [!summary]
> Movable type made copying cheap, and cheap copies changed who could argue in public. The press did not cause the Reformation alone, but it made it impossible to stop.

## My position
1. **Print did not cause the Reformation, but it made it impossible to stop.** → [[Did print cause the Reformation]], [[Reformation]]
2. **Printers were businessmen first; they printed what sold.** *(draft)* → [[Information wants to be cheap]]

## 1. How print spread
Within fifty years of the [[Gutenberg Bible]], presses ran in more than 250 European towns (Druckorte). Print followed trade routes, not borders.
→ [[Spread of print]]

## 2. Print and the Reformation
Luther's pamphlets were cheap, short and in German, and printers reprinted whatever sold: see [[Information wants to be cheap]] and [[Did print cause the Reformation]].

> [!claude] A rival view
> Elizabeth Eisenstein (*The Printing Press as an Agent of Change*, 1979) gives the press the leading role; Andrew Pettegree argues that pamphlets mattered more than books.

## How my view changed
- **2026-10-20, position 1:** I thought: Print caused the Reformation. What changed it: Earlier reformers failed without a press, but the press alone convinced nobody.
